links.outcome: Overlap between public benchmark task mix and real clinician query mix
links.effect: Median of 58 benchmarks had no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, less than an even spread across categories; clinical-practice-style suites were no closer than frontier-report benchmarks.
links.quote: Benchmark scores therefore say little about how clinical AI performs on most of the work it is actually given, and evaluation should be matched to real clinical use.

links.outcome: Whether benchmark items resemble real deployment use of an LLM assistant
links.effect: Documentation and administration were 36.2% and knowledge retrieval 28.9% of 127,833 real queries; diagnosis 3.7%; the median benchmark had no documentation requests and shared 31% of the real task mix.
links.quote: Applying RCQ-Map to 58 public benchmarks drawn from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports, which we assemble into the Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas, showed that the median benchmark contained no documentation requests and shared 31% of the task mix of real use, less than an even spread across task categories would.

unlisted_practices: Characterizing real-world clinician query logs with a task/intent/answerability/harm framework to design deployment-representative evaluation

screen.reason: Analyzed 127,833 real-world queries from thousands of clinicians during an institutional LLM assistant roll-out to compare real clinical usage patterns against standard AI benchmark evaluations.
